title: “Anti-siphon valve” can mean several products—start with the water system
description: Separate irrigation anti-siphon valves, faucet vacuum breakers, toilet fill valves, and unrelated fuel uses before following repair advice.
prompt: Where is the anti-siphon valve installed?
answer: In irrigation, the term often describes a control valve combined with atmospheric backflow protection. The correct route depends on location, pressure pattern, and whether it is part of potable-water protection.
urgency: Do not use fuel, automotive, or toilet instructions for an irrigation water-control device. Keep atmospheric vents unobstructed.
diagramAlt: Irrigation anti-siphon valve with control valve and raised atmospheric vent
identifiers: Irrigation units often combine a solenoid or manual valve with a raised vent.
Faucet devices attach at hose threads.
Toilet anti-siphon features are inside the tank and are a different task.

choices.label: Raised beside sprinkler valves
choices.detail: Use the irrigation installation and leak path.

choices.label: Inside a toilet tank
choices.detail: This portfolio does not cover toilet fill-valve repair.

steps.title: Name the water system
steps.body: Irrigation, hose connection, fixture, and fuel uses must be separated.

steps.title: Find the atmospheric opening
steps.body: Confirm whether the device admits air and where downstream shutoffs sit.

steps.title: Use the matching service path
steps.body: Do not transfer instructions between device families.

safeChecks: Record the model and voltage if a solenoid is present.
Observe whether leakage occurs only during operation.
notThisDevice: Automotive fuel anti-siphon products are outside scope.
Toilet fill valves are outside this device portfolio.
A PVB is a separate testable assembly.
evidenceNote: This route intentionally filters mixed search intent before applying water-system guidance.
